sysd-reliab-016.caption: Each factor is a different kind of evidence, with examples from each.
rows: ID card, security token, cell phone

sysd-reliab-020.caption: A login is checked by hashing the entered password with the stored salt and comparing hashes.
sysd-reliab-020.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[User enters password] --> B[Fetch the user's salt]
B --> C[Append salt, then hash]
C --> D{Hashes match?}
D -->|yes| E[Password is valid]
D -->|no| F[Password is not valid]

sysd-reliab-023.caption: The flow runs from the client's request to the resource server's reply, in five steps.
rows: Asks the authorization server for authorization, naming the scopes it wants
Authenticates the client; the resource owner grants access
Redirects back with an authorization code or an access token
Presents the access token to the resource server
Validates the token and returns the resources

sysd-reliab-132.caption: Each grant type suits a different kind of client and carries its own trade-off.
rows: The owner's credentials never reach the client
Exposes the token; no refresh token
Highly trusted clients, such as the device OS
No refresh token should be included

sysd-reliab-032.caption: A JWT is three Base64url-encoded parts joined with periods.

sysd-reliab-025.caption: In single sign-on the application sends the user to the identity provider and waits for its response.
sysd-reliab-025.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[User requests a resource] --> B[Application redirects to identity provider]
B --> C[User signs in]
C --> D[Identity provider sends SSO response]
D --> E[Application grants access]

sysd-reliab-125.caption: Kerberos trades tickets in four steps, and the password is never sent.
rows: The client authenticates and gets a ticket-granting ticket (TGT)
The client sends the TGT and gets a service ticket and session keys
The client presents the service ticket with its request
The service replies with the timestamp encrypted under the session key

sysd-q-029.caption: The API server reads the cache and the database, and takes each new key from the Key Generation Service.
sysd-q-029.mermaid:
flowchart TD
V[Visitor] --> L[Load balancer]
L --> A[API server]
A -->|checks first| C[(Cache)]
A -->|on a miss| D[(URL database)]
A -->|gets a key| K[Key Generation Service]
K --> E[(Key database)]

sysd-q-062.caption: Writes and reads take separate paths through the Web Server, and the logs feed analytics.
sysd-q-062.mermaid:
flowchart TD
C[Client] --> W[Web Server]
W -->|create| WA[Write API server]
W -->|view| RA[Read API server]
WA --> S[(SQL Database)]
WA --> O[(Object Store)]
RA --> S
RA --> O
W -.->|logs, MapReduce| A[(Analytics Database)]
